properties.rationale:
Reported by Alex 2026-08-29 (art:grok-shell-feedback-2026-08-29): after recording a ChangeEvent for a code change, capturing the same idea as a Requirement was refused naming that ChangeEvent, and a Decision restating a Capability was refused naming the Capability. The served instructions ASK for both records, so an agent following the loop honestly tripped the guard every time — his words, "distinct_from works; it is just the default path now."

🛑 THE REFUSAL WAS KEPT ON PURPOSE, AND THE OTHER REPAIR WAS REJECTED. Excluding cross-type pairs from the filter would have removed the friction and also removed a real catch when an agent genuinely duplicates an idea across layers — trading a false alarm for a silent miss, which is the failure this guard was built to stop. Nobody has counted how often a cross-type hit IS a real duplicate, so suppressing the check would act on an unmeasured assumption.

🛑 SO THIS DOES NOT REACH THE CAUSE, AND SAYS SO. fact:the-near-match-filter-has-no-node-type-term stays OPEN and stays literally true: the selection is still `not-itself AND score-above-floor`, with no type term. What changed is the WORDING, one layer later. That is the conservative half of the repair and it matches how the guard was justified — refuse_unless_deliberate is documented as forcing a CHOICE, never as preventing a write.

Root-caused with the root-cause skill; pinned by two tests written first and OBSERVED FAILING — cross-type FAILED and same-type PASSED against the unfixed code, which is the split that shows the tests discriminate rather than merely rejecting current behaviour.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: The search-before-you-add guard now words its refusal according to whether the near-match is the SAME TYPE as the node being created. A same-type hit reads as before and offers SHARPEN. A hit of another type is described as a different KIND of record, says that recording what shipped and recording what must stay true are different acts on the same work, and does NOT offer sharpening — calling `add_requirement` with a ChangeEvent's id is not a route that exists. `refuse_unless_deliberate` takes the created node's type; the four constructors that refuse (Requirement, Capability, Component, Decision) pass it.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From the dev_storyflow agent's 2026-09-24 entry (art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27), written after add_capability was refused over a dated finding. In the reporter's words: "Opportunity: cross-type near-matches as a note on success rather than a refusal, keeping refusal for same-type matches."

WHAT EXISTS TODAY. 14 cross-type pairs already behave exactly this way: PRESCRIBED_LAYER_PAIRS in capture.rs, where the match comes back in search_first.near_matches on a write that succeeded. Every OTHER cross-type pair refuses. Measured on 0.72.0 (fact:root-cause-a-dated-finding-blocks-four-intent-constructors-because-an-unlisted-cross-type-pair-refuses-2026-09-28): one TemporalFact refuses add_capability, add_requirement, add_design_rule and add_component, and is only a note for add_decision.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) THE REPORTER'S. Every cross-type near-match is a note on success, and only a same-type match refuses. This replaces the list with a rule. Cheap: one filter in the shared refuse_unless_deliberate, and the near-match report survives unchanged.
(b) A NARROWER RULE. An OBSERVATION record (TemporalFact, ChangeEvent, Verification) never refuses an INTENT write, while intent↔intent cross-type pairs stay on the list. That answers this report's class (a dated record against intent) without reopening the intent-layer pairs.
(c) KEEP THE LIST and add TemporalFact↔{Capability, Requirement, DesignRule, Component} on today's evidence. This is the path taken four times already (08-31, 09-01, 09-05, 09-16).

WHAT IS KNOWN ABOUT EACH (findings, not a ranking). (a) and (b) are stated rules, so a class test can pin them. (c) cannot be pinned as a class, because it is a list. The 2026-09-16 root cause called (c) "a hand-maintained allowlist standing in for a rule the design already states". (b) keeps a catch for an agent restating a Requirement as a Capability-shaped DesignRule, for example; (a) does not.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, recorded beside the idea rather than against it. chg:a-cross-type-near-match-is-named-as-a-layer considered option (a) on 2026-08-29 and REJECTED it: "Excluding cross-type pairs from the filter would have removed the friction and also removed a real catch when an agent genuinely duplicates an idea across layers — trading a false alarm for a silent miss." The refusal's own text still says a node that only restates another "can wear a different type". The 19/0 non-duplicate count comes from agents grading their own writes, so it is a lower bound on the false-positive rate, not a proven zero, and nobody has audited it.

AGAINST THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT: the list has had to grow for field reports five times. bhome showed agents pre-empting with distinct_from on every write, which is the silent miss arriving by another route and leaving no record. The refusal's own first sentence concedes the hit is "not a near-duplicate". And a TemporalFact is a dated observation, so an intent node can never be the same record written twice.

properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. @ajs, 2026-10-14: "I'm curious if we can use flo2 to solve: navier Stokes", citing https://openai.com/index/navier-stokes-solution/ and https://www.scientificamerican.com/article/openais-blockbuster-navier-stokes-proof-isnt-what-we-thought-it-was/.

The articles were NOT read: his brainstorm rule is "don't start building or researching". The method is a separate question, dec:idea-flo2-holds-a-proof-as-a-design-reflow2-records-the-equations-and-a-model-reasons-the-steps, and this one is only worth anything if that method exists.

OPTIONS, none chosen:
(a) NAVIER–STOKES ITSELF as the trial: design the proof attempt in flo2 and see how far the structure and the checks carry it.
(b) DESIGN THE PUBLISHED CLAIM, NOT A NEW PROOF: record the structure of the claimed Navier–Stokes result as a design (theorem, lemmas, assumptions, who checked each step), to see whether flo2 shows plainly what is proven and what is not. This is a reading of someone else's argument, not an attempt to solve the problem.
(c) A SMALLER THEOREM WITH A KNOWN PROOF FIRST, chosen so a person can tell whether the design kept every step honest. Examples: an energy estimate for a simpler PDE, or a classical result with a checkable proof.
(d) HIS OWN THESIS DERIVATION: the multiple-hypothesis test and the multi-frame accuracy math, already flo2-calc's worked case for "designing the math up front" (g). He can judge every step himself.

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- THE TARGET IS AN OPEN MILLENNIUM PRIZE PROBLEM. The existence and smoothness of solutions to the 3D incompressible Navier–Stokes equations is one of the Clay Institute's seven. As a trial of flo2, (a) has no checkable success: nobody here can judge a claimed proof, and a failure teaches little about flo2 itself.
- AN OVERCLAIM IS THE REAL RISK. A design that looks complete can read as a proof. The second headline he cited is about exactly that kind of gap between a claim and what was shown. Any public "flo2 solved X" would meet the same scrutiny. Option (b) turns that risk into the trial: it tests whether flo2 makes the gap visible.
- IT CAME FROM READING. rule:an-idea-from-reading-waits-for-a-real-use-before-it-is-built (advisory) says the default is to wait for a real use. (d), and Chris's argument (dec:idea-chris-designs-an-argument-for-and-against-as-a-first-trial), are real uses that test the same machinery.

SIZE, plainly (a finding, not a decision):
- (d): small. The case exists, and he can judge it.
- (c): small to moderate, depending on the theorem.
- (b): moderate. It needs the claimed proof read closely, and a mathematician's eye to judge it.
- (a): an open research problem, unbounded, and not a build at all.

2026-10-14, LATER: ANTHONY SKETCHES A LADDER. Still brainstorming.

IN HIS WORDS: "what do you recommend for our trial proof? something straightforward and already proven, so that we can compare the results to something previously done? then we can fix any shortcomings we identify in the trial. then try a more challenging proof?"

So the question is now which proofs make the rungs:
- a known proof first;
- its shortcomings fixed;
- then harder proofs;
- Navier–Stokes stays the far end, and is not the first trial.

WHAT A FIRST RUNG SHOULD EXERCISE (a sketch to test). Each item names the requirement it tests:
- a lemma chain: conclusions that are premises of later steps (C, chains);
- more than one rule: contradiction, induction, case split (C, the named rule);
- definitions and hypotheses as premises (D: the terms an agent must recognise);
- two independent proofs of one result, so a result is concluded by more than one Inference and losing one proof only WEAKENS it (C: "any" across inferences);
- a false conjecture refuted by a counterexample (B: CONTRADICTS, and the claims resting on it fall);
- who confirmed each step (B).

CANDIDATES, smallest first. Citations are from memory and NOT checked; the trial must check each one against its source before relying on it.
(e) √2 IS IRRATIONAL. Proof by contradiction, about 8 steps, with one lemma (if n² is even then n is even). A warm-up: it exercises contradiction and a lemma, and little else.
(f) THERE ARE INFINITELY MANY PRIMES (Euclid, Elements IX.20), with three side pieces:
  - its lemma, "every integer greater than 1 has a prime divisor" (by strong induction, or the least divisor);
  - a SECOND, independent proof, such as Goldbach's via pairwise-coprime Fermat numbers, so the result has two derivations;
  - a FALSE SIDE CONJECTURE: "n² + n + 41 is prime for every n". It holds for n = 0 to 39 and fails at n = 40 (40² + 40 + 41 = 41²). flo2-calc can evaluate those forty cases, which shows that EVALUATING IS NOT PROVING, and one counterexample refutes it.
  About 15 to 25 records. Every requirement C, B and D would be exercised once.
(g) THE FUNDAMENTAL THEOREM OF ARITHMETIC: existence by strong induction; uniqueness through Euclid's lemma, which rests on Bézout's identity, which rests on the division algorithm. A deeper dependency chain (about 40 to 60 records). Break Bézout and check that exactly the uniqueness half falls.
(h) A STEP TOWARD FLUIDS: uniqueness of solutions to the heat equation by the ENERGY METHOD. This is the technique family used in Navier–Stokes theory (energy estimates), with integrals and inequalities as premises. It tests whether prose statements of analysis still give a usable proof graph.
(i) His thesis derivation (option (d) above) fits better as a line-of-reasoning or experiment trial (requirement A) than as a proof.

HOW TO COMPARE "with something previously done" (a sketch):
- COVERAGE: every step of the reference proof has a record, and no record is unsupported.
- STRUCTURE: the dependency graph matches the reference's, with no missing premise and no circularity.
- FALL-OUT: break one premise. reflow2's broken/weakened report matches what the reference implies, worked by hand.
- CONFIRMATION: who confirmed each step is recorded.
- READ-BACK: a fresh session given only the design states the proof correctly.
- FRICTION LOG: what was awkward to record. That log is the list of shortcomings to fix before the next rung.
Run it as a three-agent trial, as before: the owner (Anthony), a designer agent, and an observer who holds the reference proof and the friction log.

PUSHBACK, RECORDED BESIDE IT:
- A FAMOUS PROOF IS MEMORISED. A model can recite Euclid instead of designing a proof. So rung (f) tests the RECORDING AND CHECKING machinery, not the reasoning. To test the method itself (design the hypothesis first, then work it step by step), give the designer only the theorem's statement and keep the reference proof with the observer. Later rungs should use results a model is less likely to recite, such as a competition problem with an official solution.
- A KNOWN ANSWER CAN HIDE A WEAK CHECK. reflow2 checks form and status, not content. A wrong step the designer marks confirmed passes. The comparison against the reference is what catches it, which is why the observer holds the reference.
- No machine checker (Lean) is in scope. The comparison is against the textbook proof, and "confirmed" means a person or the observer.

SIZE (a finding): (e) is under an hour. (f) is one session. (g) is two or three sessions. (h) is open-ended and depends on how analysis statements are written. Each rung needs C built; (f) onward needs B, for who confirmed each step.

RECOMMENDED (a finding, not a decision): (f) as the first rung, run as a three-agent trial with the designer given only the statement. Fix what its friction log shows, then (g), then (h). Navier–Stokes stays the far end.

properties.decision:
THE 2026-08-29 REPAIR NAMED ITS OWN REOPENING CONDITION, AND THE CONDITION IS NOW MET.

`chg:a-cross-type-near-match-is-named-as-a-layer` shipped the conservative half (option ② — reword the refusal when the types differ) and rejected the behavioural half (option ① — exclude the prescribed layer pairs from the filter) for exactly one stated reason: "Nobody has counted how often a cross-type hit IS a real duplicate, so suppressing the check would act on an unmeasured assumption."

`fact:twelve-near-match-refusals-across-two-designs-and-not-one-was-a-duplicate` supplies the count. 12 refusals, two independent designs with nothing in common, 12 judged distinct, 0 real duplicates. Both observers independently name the same pairings, and neither could see the other's report.

🛑 AND TWO MORE ARRIVED WHILE THIS DECISION WAS BEING WRITTEN, WHICH IS THE SHARPEST EVIDENCE IN THE FILE BECAUSE NOBODY REPORTED IT — it happened to the session doing the triage.

Attempt 1 was refused against the very measurement that motivates it: a Decision blocked by the TemporalFact it acts on. A FIFTH pairing, and the loop's own shape again — a measurement and the decision it informs are supposed to read alike.

Attempt 2, carrying `distinct_from` for that one, was refused again — against TWO DIFFERENT nodes the first refusal had not mentioned.

⭐ THAT SECOND REFUSAL BREAKS THE ONLY MITIGATION ANYONE HAS. bhome's report says it had "started passing `distinct_from` pre-emptively", and concluded that a guard routinely pre-empted has stopped being a check. This session's experience is worse than that: **you cannot pre-empt it in one call, because the near-match set is not knowable before the call and each cleared hit can reveal a fresh one.** The cost is not one extra round trip per write; it is N, unbounded, discovered one at a time, and each round trip re-sends the entire node body — here roughly 4 KB, three times. bhome recorded that same re-send cost separately (part 6) without connecting it to this.

FOUR OPTIONS, RECOMMENDED ONE FIRST.

⭐ **① SUPPRESS THE NAMED PAIRINGS, KEEP EVERY OTHER CROSS-TYPE CHECK.** Requirement↔Capability, ChangeEvent↔Decision, Decision↔Component, exploratory-Decision↔the-Decision-that-settles-it, and TemporalFact↔Decision stop refusing; every other type pair refuses exactly as today. Consequence: removes 14 of 14 observed false positives and keeps the guard armed everywhere the evidence does not reach. Cost: if one of those pairings ever IS a genuine duplication across layers, it now passes silently — but that is the failure the pre-emption habit already produces, without leaving a record.
② **RAISE THE BAR FOR THOSE PAIRINGS RATHER THAN REMOVING IT** — refuse only on a much higher similarity score. Keeps a catch for near-verbatim copies. Cost: a threshold nobody has data to set, and `fact:the-near-match-filter-has-no-node-type-term` already establishes that no ratio can separate a ChangeEvent from the Requirement behind it, because they SHOULD score alike.
③ **DISSOLVE IT INSTEAD OF TUNING IT** — `dec:idea-should-a-creation-call-carry-its-own-golden-thread` proposes `add_requirement`/`add_capability` taking `project_id` and `satisfies` inline, so the pair is created in ONE call and the second write never happens. Fixes the largest pairing at the root and removes 22 of 44 measured boilerplate edge writes. Does nothing for the other four pairings.
④ **DO NOTHING.** The guard stays armed and stays pre-empted: the false positives continue AND the check is not actually running. Strictly worse than ①.

⭐ RECOMMENDATION: ① NOW AND ③ SEPARATELY, not one instead of the other. ③ is the better fix for one pairing and is a larger piece of work; ① is available at the line that already has the type pair in hand (capture.rs:190) and needs no new lookup, plumbing or vocabulary.

📌 ONE REPAIR IS WORTH DOING UNDER EVERY OPTION INCLUDING ④: make the refusal return the WHOLE near-match set rather than one layer of it, so `distinct_from` can be answered once. Attempt 2 proves it does not today, and that is a bug independent of how the guard is tuned.
properties.name: OPEN — the cross-type near-match repair was parked for want of a count. The count is now 12 refusals, 0 duplicates. Does the behavioural half proceed?
properties.rationale:
THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENT, because a recommendation with no counterweight reads as steering:

The measurement has a real weakness and it should be weighed rather than waved past. Both field observers are AGENTS, both judged their OWN writes, and an agent that has decided its write is distinct is not a neutral referee — 12/0 is a lower bound on the false-positive rate, not a proven zero. Nobody has audited the 12 to see whether any was a duplicate the agent talked itself past. If even one was, option ① makes that class permanently invisible.

Against that: the guard is documented as `refuse_unless_deliberate` — forcing a CHOICE, never preventing a write — so it never had the power to stop a determined duplicate. And option ④ preserves the appearance of a check and none of its effect, which is the worst state of the four.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING BEFORE DECIDING: the 2026-08-29 repair is not wasted work under any option. The rewording is what let musicjug say "that sentence told me instantly which of the two cases I was in" — the message change earned its keep independently of whether the behaviour now changes too.

⚠️ AND A NOTE ON THE EVIDENCE'S PROVENANCE, since this design cares about it: the two in-session refusals are the only ones here NOT self-reported by an agent grading its own work. They were incurred, not observed, and they would have been recorded identically whichever way they fell.

properties.source: @ajs, 2026-10-17: "do 1, 2 and 6 first" (fix 1), with his choices "Note, never refuse" for cross-type and for within a proof
properties.statement:
When a create or revise finds an existing record whose wording is close, reflow2 handles it as follows:
- WRITES and reports the match beside the result (search_first.near_matches, naming each match and its type) when the match is of a different node type, or when both records belong to a line of reasoning (a statement carrying a statement_kind, or an Inference).
- REFUSES, as today, only for a same-type match outside a line of reasoning, with the same three answers: sharpen, distinct_from, replaces.
- The hand-kept list of exempt cross-type pairs is replaced by this rule, and a class test pins the rule.
Measured case to carry over: proof-trial rung 2 on design bbcd344a71ff1cbd, where about 19 creates were refused. A statement there was refused three times against three different nodes, and distinct_from lists of 15–18 ids were needed. Under this rule, recording the same proof needs no distinct_from at all.

properties.statement:
Triage of art:dev-reflow2-two-agent-exercise-feedback-2026-09-29, item I27 (friction-log entry #14).

Walked briefly:
- Precedent: chg:a-cross-type-near-match-is-named-as-a-layer and this idea. The 2026-09-16 and 09-28 root causes of cross-type refusals: fact:root-cause-the-guard-still-refuses-thread-pairs-because-the-prescribed-set-was-built-from-evidence-and-the-evidence-for-capability-component-arrived-today and fact:root-cause-a-dated-finding-blocks-four-intent-constructors-because-an-unlisted-cross-type-pair-refuses-2026-09-28.

The reporter's words: "A capability 'Searches across …' was flagged as near the component 'Per-user search index'. Cost: noise, ~300 chars."
- The write succeeded, so this is the NOTE path (working as designed since the chg), not a refusal.
- The pair is a Capability and the Component it is ALLOCATED to. That is a thread pair: the two SHOULD read alike, because one delivers the other.
- The report's own reading, "noise", is right about the cost and wrong about the cause. The guard did what it was built to do.
- The open question is whether a thread pair should produce any note at all. This idea's option of noting only same-type matches would have made it silent.

Not reproduced here: the exact note text and whether allocated_to was passed in the same call are from the designer's log, not measured. So confidence is 0.6.

properties.name: Proof trial rung 2 (fundamental theorem of arithmetic) on 0.86.0: the logic is recorded and checked faithfully; recording a proof is still costly, and the reasoning read-back elides its prose
properties.source: the trial's observer (Claude, this session) with its designer and reader agents; Anthony owned the design and confirmed nothing
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-10-17. Design: flo2.io bbcd344a71ff1cbd ("fundamental theorem of arithmetic (proof trial)"), run on reflow2 0.86.0, flo2 at 4306832 and flo2-calc 0.9.0. Three-agent trial: Anthony as owner; a designer given ONLY the statement; an observer holding the reference proof, checked against its sources (Wikipedia's fundamental theorem of arithmetic and Euclid's lemma; Euclid VII.30–31; Gauss art. 14 and 16; the Hilbert-number counterexample 441 = 9·49 = 21·21 computed by the observer). A fresh read-back agent came last. 48 inference steps, all unconfirmed; the owner confirmed none.

WHAT THE 0.86.0 FIXES DID, each checked by the observer's own call:
- A lost premise reads UNSUPPORTED, never false.
  - propagate_from on Bézout makes Euclid's lemma → uniqueness line 1 → (before round 2) the theorem unsupported, while existence holds: exactly the uniqueness half falls.
  - After the second line was added, losing Bézout leaves uniqueness still_supported_by the least-counterexample line.
  - Losing EXISTENCE takes line 2 only (uniqueness still_supported_by line 1). The theorem goes unsupported, because existence is half of it. That is the hand-worked asymmetry, exactly.
- 9 + 1 suppositions are recorded as assumed and all discharged.
- independent_of / independent_except holds between the two lines, and a deliberately under-named exception fails.
- 4 owner questions were raised by ask_question (origin asker, no gap).
- The refuted conjecture reads "refuted", not as a defect.
- A computed fact holds ONLY through its kept calc record: "passing through its kept record art:file-hilbert-441-counterexample-calc-json, and its findings state the result". The record is kept with its sha256 by flo2's helper keep, and rerun_record reproduces it.
- statement_kind reads conjecture / proposition / definition as intended.
- The fresh reader rebuilt the whole proof correctly in 11 calls and found no wrong step.

FRICTION STILL MET, most costly first. These are observations; no cause is asserted.
1. The near-duplicate check refused about 19 creates over two rounds, often ACROSS types: a Requirement against an Inference, the Project or an unrelated step. It got worse as the design grew (one statement was refused 3×, against 3 different nodes), so distinct_from lists of 15–18 guessed ids were needed. A Requirement is refused where a Constraint only warns, and distinct_from drops ids not yet created.
2. reasoning_report elided ALL 169 prose fields to "…" for the reader: budget_chars 120000 was lowered to a ~29k cap, and 25 of 66 claims came back. The statements and warrants, which are the proof, were readable only through scan_nodes node_type Inference.
3. A short textbook proof cost 83 records in round 1; each induction needs about 6.
4. A supposition, and a contradiction node (⊥), read truth "holds" on its own. There is no falsum and no form for a case split's exhaustiveness. Variable letters are global, so generalization lists mix unrelated lemmas.
5. The design-a-proof skill says leave `kind` alone, while detect_gaps raises encoding_undecided on all 34 statements.
6. loop_status says "NO REAL RESULT HAS EVER COME BACK / no_executable_form" after rerun_record reproduced the kept record. It also lists questions_put_to_them [] while counting 4 unanswered.
7. reasoning_report with a small limit returns rests_on [] and stated_foundations [], which reads as "rests on nothing".
8. detect_defects names Lemmas 6 and 7 as single points of failure, but not strong induction or the six foundations every line also rests on.
9. find_tools does not rank propagate_from for "what still holds if a premise were lost", and total_impacted counts upstream nodes.
10. Genesis and the pressing questions stay software-shaped for a proof: platform, artifact standard, closure criterion, taxonomy.
FLO2-SIDE, read_my_design_back: by_kind omits Inference; refuted conjectures fall outside the claim counts ("unproven 0, objections standing 0"); and step counts disagree between the theorem (41) and uniqueness (47).
INSTALL NOTE, from the flo2 move: reflow2's 0.86.0 notes say tantivy 0.27 rebuilds no search index, but flo2's design rebuilt it once on first open (fields_changed true, 1,487 nodes), with identical results.

The observer's file is in the session scratchpad, fta-trial/OBSERVER.md. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_019Xbw6PG9mXJiU2Sb421fnq
